decisions.reason: The cited filtered-space definition explicitly starts at zero, whereas the algorithm supplied only times t>=1. This is a nonfatal indexing-interface omission: every increasing positive-time filtration extends by F_0={empty,Omega}, with no change to any update or oracle law. Changed only the filtration index to t>=0; the procedure still starts at x_1, has finite positive steps, and returns x_1 through x_{N+1} without moment assumptions.

F9 and F10 omitted essential smoothness and initialization/lower-bound hypotheses from their standalone summaries. This is nonfatal for this example: f(x)=x^2/2 is C1 with exactly 1-Lipschitz gradient and global lower bound zero, x_0 is deterministic, and all directions and iterates have finite moments on the sign cube. Restored both complete cited interfaces and explicitly checked them in 2.2; also made the y_s=x_{s-1} algorithm reindexing explicit in 1.1. Direct prefix averaging verifies zero sign means, variance sigma^2, the mean recurrence and variance geometric sum. Their sum gives the exact displayed second moment and limit, including b=0, sigma=0 and N=1. The two theorem bounds use Delta=x_0^2/2 and the correct step thresholds. Example and claim strength are unchanged.

The algorithm names its first iterate x_1, while this example starts at x_0; the original F1 invocation omitted that relabeling. This is nonfatal because the update law is invariant under shifting time and the singleton filtration satisfies both index conventions. Verification 1.1 now applies the actual finite-horizon procedure to y_s=x_{s-1}, H_s=G_{s-1}=-y_s and the constant filtration, recovering every claimed zero-based update without changing the Example. Induction gives x_t=(1+alpha)^t x_0 !=0; f(x_1)=(1+alpha)^2 f(x_0)>f(x_0), and the conditional direction-gradient product is -x_t^2<0, excluding every positive alignment constant. The deterministic mean and zero variance are immediate on the singleton; AC is retained only for comparison with the theorem.
